evals.prompt: I have a new Git project that will contain a .env file and config/secrets.yml for storing database passwords and API keys. I want to use git-crypt to encrypt these files, then share the key with my colleague Wang (GPG email: wang@example.com). Walk me through the setup step by step.
evals.expected_output: Explain initialization, rules active before git add, staging and verifying ciphertext, and the requested GPG grant. Track .gitattributes; a separate earlier commit is optional. Explain add-gpg-user auto-commit behavior.

assertions.text: Includes the git-crypt init command
Shows correct .gitattributes with filter=git-crypt diff=git-crypt syntax
Requires encryption rules and filters to be active before sensitive files are staged; permits .gitattributes and encrypted files in the same commit.
Includes .gitattributes !filter !diff to prevent encrypting .gitattributes itself
Uses git-crypt add-gpg-user to share access with the colleague

evals.prompt: My repo already has a credentials/ directory with several JSON files containing tokens for various services. They were pushed in plaintext without any encryption. Now I want to encrypt that directory with git-crypt. How should I handle this? What about the leaked history?
evals.expected_output: Advise rotating exposed tokens, configure credentials/**, stage encrypted replacements, verify the index, and only verify HEAD after a requested commit. Historical plaintext remains; discuss separately authorized cleanup.

assertions.text: Mentions git-crypt status -f to fix/encrypt files that should be encrypted
Uses credentials/** (double star) not credentials/* for recursive directory encryption
Warns that plaintext versions remain in Git history even after encryption
Suggests git filter-repo or BFG Repo-Cleaner for separately authorized history cleanup; does not silently rewrite or force-push.
Advises rotating/revoking the already-exposed tokens

evals.prompt: Our team has frontend and backend groups. Frontend needs access to frontend/config/.env, backend needs access to backend/secrets/ for database connection info. I don't want frontend to see backend's database passwords, and I don't want backend to see frontend's third-party API keys. Can git-crypt do this? How do I set it up?
evals.expected_output: Should introduce git-crypt's multiple key feature: create named keys with git-crypt init -k frontend and git-crypt init -k backend, use filter=git-crypt-frontend and filter=git-crypt-backend in .gitattributes, then use add-gpg-user -k to grant per-key access to different users

assertions.text: Uses git-crypt init -k to create named keys (e.g. frontend, backend)
Uses filter=git-crypt-KEYNAME syntax in .gitattributes (not just filter=git-crypt)
Uses git-crypt add-gpg-user -k KEYNAME to grant per-key access
Explains that git-crypt unlock auto-detects which key the user has access to

evals.prompt: I ran git-crypt status -f after configuring encryption for an existing tracked .env. It says it staged an encrypted version. git show HEAD:.env still contains the old plaintext. Is the repair broken? Explain without printing any secret values.
evals.expected_output: Explain the difference between the index and HEAD. Verify staged ciphertext without printing secrets, commit only if requested, and explain that historical plaintext remains.

assertions.text: Recognizes that status -f updates the index, not HEAD, and checks the staged version.
Does not claim the existing commit or history is encrypted and does not require rerunning repair solely because HEAD is old.
Does not print decrypted contents or export keys to stdout.

evals.prompt: This repo already uses git-crypt and its tracked secrets are encrypted. Please verify config/secrets.yml. Do not initialize keys, stage files, commit, or grant access.
evals.expected_output: Use read-only status and stored-blob checks for the requested file. Existing tracking alone is not evidence of a secret leak.

assertions.text: Does not initialize a new key, repair the index, commit, or grant access.
Does not demand credential rotation merely because the file is tracked.
Verifies encryption without revealing decrypted content; generic binary classification alone is insufficient.

evals.prompt: Two tracked files, .env and other.env, need re-encryption after their git-crypt rules changed. Only repair the staged version of .env; do not touch other.env or create a commit.
evals.expected_output: Force the clean filter to run for the requested tracked path only, verify its index blob, and leave other.env and HEAD unchanged.

assertions.text: Avoids a repository-wide status -f repair and stages only .env.
Uses git add --renormalize -- .env or another verified way to reapply the clean filter to the unchanged tracked file.
Verifies staged ciphertext and does not claim a new commit was made.
